To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
1) energy expenditure is increased in patients with chronic kidney disease (CKD), and 2) energy expenditure is related to the severity of the disease.

1) the energy expenditure (EE) is increased by 15% in CKD patients compared to controls, and 2) the increase of EE is associated with the increase of the resting metabolic rate (RMR), and 3) the RMR increase is associated with the increased protein intake.
The energy intake of CKD patients with an eGFR between 10 and 30 mL/min/1.73 m² and an estimated protein intake below 0.8 g/kg/day is 10% to 15% higher than the estimated energy expenditure.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of novel methods for the determination of the energy expenditure in CKD patients.
the development of a novel, low-cost and portable device that can be utilized in the home environment to measure energy expenditure (EE) and physical activity (PA) levels.
the energy expenditure of patients with chronic kidney disease and its association with the nutritional status and clinical parameters.

this study shows that the energy expenditure in CKD individuals is increased and that it correlates with the severity of the disease.
